question: Which type of molecules show dipole-dipole interaction?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Molecules possessing permanent dipole**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dipole-dipole interactions occur between molecules that have permanent dipoles.
 
• The positive end of one polar molecule attracts the negative end of another polar molecule.
 
• These interactions are stronger than London dispersion forces but weaker than hydrogen bonds.
 
• Examples of molecules showing dipole-dipole interactions include hydrogen chloride (HCl) and sulfur dioxide (SO2).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Transient Dipole:**

 
 
• Transient dipoles are temporary dipoles that arise due to the momentary distribution of electrons within a molecule.
 
• They are responsible for London dispersion forces, which are present in all molecules but are the only type of intermolecular force in non-polar molecules.
 
 
 
• **Ionic Molecules:**
 
 
• Ionic molecules consist of positively and negatively charged ions.
 
• The intermolecular forces between ionic molecules are known as ionic bonds, which are significantly stronger than dipole-dipole interactions.
 
 
 
• **Non-Polar Molecules:**
 
 
• Non-polar molecules have no permanent dipole moment.
 
• The primary intermolecular forces in non-polar molecules are London dispersion forces.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen Bonds:**
 
 
• Hydrogen bonds are a special type of dipole-dipole interaction.
 
• They occur when hydrogen is directly bonded to highly electronegative elements like fluorine, oxygen, or nitrogen.
 
• Hydrogen bonds are stronger than regular dipole-dipole interactions due to the high polarity of the involved bonds.
